investigation.title: local-agent-runtime eval failure: upstream model provider returned 424 provider_account_unavailable, blocking all required evidence collection
investigation.summary: The local-agent-runtime eval check failed because POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test returned HTTP 502, wrapping an upstream 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable. Because the LLM call never completed, the harness produced no response payload, leaving all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent and the message assertion ("hello from aura") unverifiable. This is an eval-infrastructure failure scoped to the model-provider connectivity layer; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The AURA backend was transiently unable to reach the configured model provider at the time of the eval run (2026-10-02T13:22:15–21Z). The runtime test endpoint surfaced this as a 424 Failed Dependency with code provider_account_unavailable, which the harness translated into a 502 bad_gateway response. Because the LLM invocation failed before producing any output, the probe received an empty evidence object and could not satisfy the local-agent-runtime expected-output contract (requiredEvidence: orgId, agentId, model, provider, message; assertion: message containsIgnoreCase "hello from aura"). The failure is localized to the model-provider reachability path exercised by POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test; agent creation and permissions checks on the same run both passed, confirming that AURA's agent management APIs and auth layer were healthy at the same timestamp.

investigation.title: project-agent-chat-stream Eval Failure: Model Provider 424 Error Blocks Session Persistence and Text Generation Across All Project Agent Checks
investigation.summary: The desktop-release eval for project-agent-chat-stream failed at 2026-10-02T13:22:35Z with an HTTP 424 Failed Dependency error (code: provider_account_unavailable, support_id: 3d40c07e526d), indicating AURA's backend could not reach the upstream model provider during the eval run. Because the model provider was unreachable, the chat stream never produced text output, no session was persisted, and the required evidence fields sessionId, sessionCount, and expectedPhrase were never populated, causing the contract assertions to fail.
investigation.rootCause: The upstream model provider was unavailable at the time the eval ran, as reported by the API's own error body (code: provider_account_unavailable). This caused the project/session chat stream to terminate with an error frame before any text_delta, session persistence, or phrase generation could occur. The failure is localized to the model provider connectivity layer on the desktop-release runtime path; it is an eval-time infrastructure signal, not a confirmed user-traffic incident. All four sibling checks in the project-agent-workflows feature also failed within the same ~3-minute window, each exhibiting the same early-termination frame pattern (progress → session_ready → assistant_message_start → error → message), consistent with a shared provider-availability dependency rather than individual check logic regressions.

investigation.rootCause: The upstream model provider was unavailable (HTTP 424, code: provider_account_unavailable) during the eval window starting at 2026-10-02T13:22:35.209Z. Because the agent could not reach the model, it could not generate tool calls for write_file, read_file, or run_command. The stream terminated with an error frame instead of tool-use frames, leaving toolNames empty and all tool-outcome assertions false. This is an eval-infrastructure signal of a transient or ongoing model provider outage; no user-traffic or incident evidence is present in the packet to confirm a broader production impact.

investigations.title: Project Agent Subagent Roundtrip Eval Failure: task Tool Not Invoked, childRunId Never Emitted (desktop-release)
investigations.summary: The eval check project-agent-subagent-roundtrip failed on desktop-nightly-macos-aarch64 because the parent agent's chat stream never invoked the task tool, never spawned a subagent, and consequently never emitted a childRunId — the sole missing required evidence item. All four sibling checks under project-agent-workflows also failed, with two (project-agent-chat-stream and session-share-public-read) returning HTTP 424 provider_account_unavailable errors, and two others (project-agent-tool-roundtrip and project-agent-a2a-roundtrip) showing empty toolNames arrays identical in shape to the primary failure.
investigations.rootCause: The root cause is uncertain but the earliest violated boundary is the model provider layer: the parent agent chat stream received an error frame (evidenced by "error" appearing in frameTypes) and produced no tool calls (toolNames: [], taskToolUsed: false), which prevented subagent spawning and childRunId emission entirely. Two sibling checks explicitly surface HTTP 424 provider_account_unavailable (code: provider_account_unavailable, support_id=3d40c07e526d and support_id=5c50bd4a7d34), indicating the model provider was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The subagent roundtrip check did not itself receive a 424 message, but the identical symptom pattern — error frame present, empty toolNames, zero tool invocations — is consistent with the agent receiving an error response from the provider before it could plan or call any tool. A secondary possibility is a tool-availability or permissions regression in the desktop-release runtime that prevented the task tool from being offered to the model, but this is less supported because the provider unavailability signal is present across siblings.

investigations.summary: The session-share-public-read eval failed because the upstream model provider returned HTTP 424 (Failed Dependency) with error code provider_account_unavailable during the initial runProjectChatTurn call, causing the runner to short-circuit before a sessionId, shareId, shareUrl, or publicMessageCount could be produced. All four sibling checks under project-agent-workflows failed in the same run window with the same 424 error pattern, confirming the model provider was unavailable to the eval harness at the time of execution.
investigations.rootCause: The model provider was unreachable from the eval harness at 2026-10-02T13:25:18–13:25:26Z, returning HTTP 424 / provider_account_unavailable (support_id=5c50bd4a7d34). The runner branch at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1848–1849 calls runProjectChatTurn first and propagates its failure immediately (chat.status === CHECK_STATUS.FAIL → return chat), so no session was created and none of the downstream share-creation or public-read steps were attempted. The missing evidence (sessionId, shareIdPresent, shareUrlPresent, publicMessageCount) is a direct consequence of this early exit, not an independent defect in the share or public-read logic.
proof: failed-check.message: HTTP 424 / provider_account_unavailable returned during the chat turn; support_id=5c50bd4a7d34; missing evidence: sessionId, shareIdPresent, shareUrlPresent, publicMessageCount.
failed-check.evidence: frameTypes include 'error' and 'message' but no 'text_delta'; textSample is empty, confirming the model never produced a completion.
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=8151, well below the 45000ms warning threshold, indicating the provider rejected the request immediately rather than timing out.

sibling.project-agent-chat-stream: same 424 / provider_account_unavailable error (support_id=3d40c07e526d) at 13:22:35Z, three minutes before the primary check, showing the condition was persistent across the run window.
sibling.project-agent-tool-roundtrip: toolNames=[], all tool assertions false, textSample empty — consistent with a provider error preventing any model response.

sibling.project-agent-a2a-roundtrip: toolNames=[], listAgentsUsed=false, sendToAgentUsed=false, delivered=false; reviewerEventsError='Timed out after 120000ms' — model never responded to either agent.
sibling.project-agent-subagent-roundtrip: taskToolUsed=false, subagentSpawned=false, sessionSubagentError='Parent chat stream did not emit a child run id' — same upstream failure propagated.
source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1841-1849: runner calls runProjectChatTurn then immediately returns on FAIL status, so share steps are never reached when the chat turn fails.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: sessionId, shareIdPresent, shareUrlPresent, publicMessageCount all absent — exactly the evidence that depends on a successful chat turn completing first.
possibleCauses: [Most likely] Transient model provider outage or capacity event at the time of the eval run: all five checks across the project-agent-workflows feature received 424 / provider_account_unavailable within a ~3-minute window, and the error message explicitly states the issue is on AURA's side, not the eval account.

[Secondary] Eval harness credential or routing misconfiguration causing the provider gateway to reject requests with 424: possible but less likely given the error message text and the fact that projectId and agentInstanceId were successfully resolved before the provider call.

recommendedNextActions: Wait for provider recovery and re-run the eval before treating this as a code regression — the 424 / provider_account_unavailable error and its presence across all five sibling checks strongly suggests a transient provider-side event.
Cross-reference support_id=5c50bd4a7d34 and support_id=3d40c07e526d with internal provider gateway incident records to confirm whether a provider outage was active during 2026-10-02T13:22–13:26Z.

If the provider has recovered and a re-run still fails, inspect the share-creation and public-read logic in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs downstream of the runProjectChatTurn call to determine whether sessionId, shareIdPresent, shareUrlPresent, or publicMessageCount are being collected and returned correctly.

Monitor the project-agent-workflows feature for continued failures across multiple run windows; if the 424 error recurs without a known provider incident, investigate whether the eval harness token or provider endpoint configuration was affected by recent changes to the eval infrastructure files.

Because session-share-public-read is marked required=false in infra/evals/status/features.json (line 130), no outage threshold is breached by this single failure; however, sustained failures across the required sibling checks (project-agent-chat-stream etc.) should be escalated if they persist.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A subsequent eval run where the provider returns 200 and the chat turn completes successfully but sessionId, shareIdPresent, shareUrlPresent, or publicMessageCount are still missing — this would indicate a defect in the share-creation or public-read logic independent of the provider error.
Provider gateway logs showing no outage or capacity event during 2026-10-02T13:22–13:26Z — this would shift suspicion to a credential, routing, or harness configuration problem.

Evidence that only session-share-public-read failed while project-agent-chat-stream passed in the same run — this would localize the fault to the share or public-read steps rather than the shared chat turn dependency.
A passing run of project-agent-chat-stream immediately after this failure window with no provider error — this would confirm the provider event was transient and the share logic was never reached.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight provider health check eval that validates the model provider returns a non-error response before any project-agent-workflows checks are attempted, allowing the runner to skip dependent checks with a clear SKIP reason rather than propagating a FAIL.

Add an eval that specifically isolates the share-creation and public-read steps using a pre-seeded session (bypassing runProjectChatTurn) so that share endpoint health can be verified independently of provider availability.

Add a provider-error classification step in the runner that distinguishes provider_account_unavailable (infrastructure) from other failure modes (auth, logic, timeout) and surfaces a distinct check status (e.g., CHECK_STATUS.INFRA_ERROR) to prevent provider outages from masking genuine regressions in share or session logic.
